\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{غالبا} (ghāliban)}{غالبا (ghāliban)}]{\ar{غالبا} (ghāliban) — usually, mostly}

\label{lesson:AR-C202-ghaliban}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a burn, then the Arabic for a stomach cramp.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{غالبا}}
\textbf{\ar{غالبا}} — \emph{ghāliban} — \textquotedblleft{}usually, mostly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{غالبا}} (\emph{ghāliban}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{gh-l-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to overcome\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ghāliban} is the active participle, \textquotedblleft{}prevailing\textquotedblright{}, with the adverb ending \emph{-an}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāliban}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāliban}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ghāliban}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a burn, then the Arabic for a stomach cramp, then say \emph{ghāliban} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{غالبا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Usually, mostly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فورا}}
\textbf{\ar{فورا}} — \emph{fawran} — \textquotedblleft{}immediately\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تاريخ} (tārīkh)}{تاريخ (tārīkh)}]{\ar{تاريخ} (tārīkh) — a date; history}

\label{lesson:AR-C202-tarikh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for immediately, then the Arabic for later.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تاريخ}}
\textbf{\ar{تاريخ}} — \emph{tārīkh} — \textquotedblleft{}a date; history\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تاريخ}} (\emph{tārīkh}) is disputed in Lane's sources: some call it arabicized, borrowed from the people of the Bible, and Lane compares Hebrew \emph{yeraḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}month\textquotedblright{}; others give it a native root \emph{ʾ-r-kh}, \textquotedblleft{}to date\textquotedblright{}. The origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}
